questions.q:
[Figure: a ray of light strikes a plane mirror; the incident ray makes an angle of 30° with the normal, the reflected ray leaves at an equal angle, and α is the angle marked between the reflected ray and the mirror surface] Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(a) Angle of reflection
(b) Value of α
(c) Angle of deviation
List-II
(i) 60°
(ii) 120°
(iii) 30°
options: a - i, b - ii, c - iii
a - ii, b - i, c - iii
a - iii, b - i, c - ii
a - iii, b - ii, c - i
questions.explanation: Angle of reflection = angle of incidence = 30° (iii). α, measured from the mirror surface, is 90°−30°=60° (i). The angle of deviation on reflection is 180°−2×30°=120° (ii).

questions.q: The direction of a ray of light incident on a concave mirror is shown by PQ, while direction in which the ray would travel after reflection is shown by four rays marked as A, B, C and D as shown in the figure. Which of the four rays correctly shows the direction of the reflected ray? [Figure: a concave mirror with pole O and focus F; a ray PQ travels parallel to the principal axis and strikes the mirror at Q; four candidate reflected rays A, B, C, D emerge from Q in different directions, with ray C passing through F]
questions.explanation: A ray travelling parallel to the principal axis must, after reflection from a concave mirror, pass through the focus F. Ray C is the one passing through F.

questions.q: The incorrect statement about refractive index for a pair of media is
options: It depends upon nature of the first medium
It depends upon nature of the second medium
It depends upon wavelength of light
It depends upon angle of incidence
questions.explanation: The refractive index for a pair of media depends on the nature of both media and on the wavelength of light, but not on the angle of incidence.

questions.q: The critical angle for a monochromatic light going from medium A to medium B is θ. If the speed of light in medium A is V, then the speed of light in medium B is
questions.explanation: At the critical angle, $\sin\theta=\dfrac{n_B}{n_A}=\dfrac{v_A}{v_B}=\dfrac{V}{v_B}$, so $v_B=\dfrac{V}{\sin\theta}$.

questions.q: From the graph of angle of deviation versus angle of incidence for an equilateral prism, the refractive index of material of prism is [Figure: graph of deviation δ vs angle of incidence i for a prism, showing minimum deviation δ$_m$ = 60° occurring at angle of incidence i = 60°]
questions.explanation: At minimum deviation, $\mu=\dfrac{\sin\left(\frac{A+\delta_m}{2}\right)}{\sin\left(\frac{A}{2}\right)}=\dfrac{\sin60^\circ}{\sin30^\circ}=\dfrac{\sqrt3/2}{1/2}=\sqrt3$ for the equilateral prism (A = 60°, δ$_m$ = 60°).

questions.q: A ray of light passes from vacuum into a medium of refractive index n. If the angle of incidence is twice the angle of refraction, then the angle of incidence in terms of refractive index is
questions.explanation: $\sin(2r)=n\sin r \Rightarrow 2\cos r = n \Rightarrow r=\cos^{-1}(n/2)$, and the angle of incidence $i=2r=2\cos^{-1}(n/2)$.

questions.q: A convex lens has power P. It is cut into two halves along its principal axis. Further one piece (out of two halves) is cut into two halves perpendicular to the principal axis as shown in figure. Choose the incorrect option for the reported lens pieces
questions.explanation: Cutting along the principal axis leaves each half (L$_1$) with the same power P as the original lens; cutting that half perpendicular to the axis instead halves the power of each smaller piece (L$_2$, L$_3$) to P/2. So the claim that L$_1$'s power is P/2 is the incorrect one.

questions.q: The image formed by an objective lens of a compound microscope is
questions.explanation: The objective forms a real, inverted and enlarged image of the object (placed just beyond its focus), which then acts as the object for the eyepiece.

questions.q: If r and r$^1$ denote the angles inside the prism having angle of prism 50° considering that during interval of time from t = 0 to t = t, r varies with time as r = 10° + t$^2$. During this time r$^1$ will vary with time as
questions.explanation: For a prism, $r+r^1=A=50^\circ$, so $r^1=50^\circ-r=50^\circ-(10^\circ+t^2)=40^\circ-t^2$.

questions.q: In determining the refractive index of a glass slab using a travelling microscope, the following readings are tabulated. (a) Reading of travelling microscope for ink mark = 5.123 cm (b) Reading of travelling microscope for ink mark through glass slab = 6.123 cm (c) Reading of travelling microscope for chalk dust on glass slab = 8.123 cm. From the data, the refractive index of a glass slab is
questions.explanation: Real thickness $=c-a=3.0$ cm; apparent thickness $=c-b=2.0$ cm. $\mu=\dfrac{\text{real depth}}{\text{apparent depth}}=\dfrac{3.0}{2.0}=1.5$.

questions.q: The final image formed by an astronomical telescope is
questions.explanation: An astronomical telescope in normal adjustment forms a virtual, inverted, and magnified final image.

questions.q: If the angle of minimum deviation is equal to angle of a prism for an equilateral prism, then the speed of light inside the prism is _____
questions.explanation: $\mu=\dfrac{\sin\frac{A+d_m}{2}}{\sin\frac{A}{2}}$; with $A=d_m=60^\circ$, $\mu=\dfrac{\sin60^\circ}{\sin30^\circ}=\sqrt3$, so $v=\dfrac{c}{\mu}=\sqrt3\times10^8\,ms^{-1}$.

questions.q: A luminous point object O is placed at a distance 2R from the spherical boundary separating two transparent media of refractive indices $n_1$ and $n_2$ as shown, where R is the radius of curvature of the spherical surface. If $n_1=\dfrac43,n_2=\dfrac32$ and R=10cm, the image is obtained at a distance from P equal to [O in medium $n_1$ at distance 2R from the vertex P of a spherical surface curving into medium $n_2$, centre of curvature C beyond P]
questions.explanation: Using $\dfrac{n_2}{v}-\dfrac{n_1}{u}=\dfrac{n_2-n_1}{R}$ with $u=-2R=-20$cm: $\dfrac{3/2}{v}-\dfrac{4/3}{-20}=\dfrac{3/2-4/3}{10}$ gives $v=-30$cm, i.e. 30 cm on the same (rarer, $n_1$) side.

questions.q: An equiconvex lens of radius of curvature 14 cm is made up of two different materials. Left half and right half of vertical portion is made up of material of refractive index 1.5 and 1.2 respectively as shown in the figure. If a point object is placed at a distance of 40 cm, calculate the image distance.
questions.explanation: Each half acts as a thin lens with $f=\dfrac{R}{2(\mu-1)}$; the two halves in parallel give an effective focal length of 20 cm, and $\dfrac1v-\dfrac1u=\dfrac1f$ with $u=-40$cm gives $v=40$cm.

questions.q: For a given pair of transparent media, the critical angle for which colour is maximum?
questions.explanation: Critical angle $\theta_c=\sin^{-1}(1/n)$ is largest for the smallest refractive index; red light has the least refractive index among visible colours, so it has the maximum critical angle.

questions.q: An equiconvex lens made of glass of refractive index $\dfrac{3}{2}$ has focal length f in air. It is completely immersed in water of refractive index $\dfrac{4}{3}$. The percentage change in the focal length is
questions.explanation: 1/f $\propto (n_{lens}/n_{medium}-1)$. In air this factor is (3/2−1)=0.5; in water it is ((3/2)/(4/3)−1)=1/8, i.e. 1/4 as large, so f becomes 4 times larger — a 300% increase.

questions.q: A point object is moving at a constant speed of 1 ms$^{-1}$ along the principal axis of a convex lens of focal length 10 cm. The speed of the image is also 1 ms$^{-1}$, when the object is at ____ cm from the optic centre of the lens.
questions.explanation: Image speed equals object speed when magnification magnitude is 1, which for a convex lens occurs when the object is at u=2f=20 cm (real, inverted, same-size image).

questions.q: For a point object, which of the following always produces virtual image in air?
questions.explanation: A convex mirror always forms a virtual, diminished, erect image for a real object placed at any distance; lenses and concave mirrors can form real images depending on object position.

questions.q: Consider a glass slab which is silvered at one side and the other side is transparent. Given the refractive index of the glass slab to be 1.5. If a ray of light is incident at an angle of 45$^\circ$ on the transparent side, the deviation of the ray of light from its initial path, when it comes out of the slab is
questions.explanation: A glass slab silvered on the back behaves like a plane mirror for the incoming ray, so the net deviation is 180$^\circ$ $-$ 2i = 180$^\circ$ $-$ 2(45$^\circ$) = 90$^\circ$.

questions.q: Focal length of a convex lens will be maximum for
questions.explanation: Since $\dfrac{1}{f}=(\mu-1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1}-\dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)$, and red light has the smallest refractive index among the given colours, it bends the least and so gives the maximum focal length.

questions.q: A ray of light passes through an equilateral glass prism in such a manner that the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of emergence and each of these angles is equal to $\dfrac{3}{4}$ of the angle of the prism. The angle of deviation is
questions.explanation: Angle of prism A = 60$^\circ$; $i=e=\dfrac{3}{4}\times60^\circ=45^\circ$. Deviation $D=i+e-A=45+45-60=30^\circ$.

questions.q: A convex lens of focal length 'f' is placed somewhere in between an object and a screen. The distance between the object and the screen is 'x'. If the numerical value of the magnification produced by the lens is 'm', then the focal length of the lens is
questions.explanation: With $u+v=x$ and $v=mu$: $u=\dfrac{x}{1+m}$, $v=\dfrac{mx}{1+m}$. Then $f=\dfrac{uv}{u+v}=\dfrac{mx}{(1+m)^2}$.

questions.q: The power of a equi-concave lens is $-$4.5 D and is made of a material of R.I. 1.6, the radii of curvature of the lens is
questions.explanation: For an equiconcave lens $R_1=-R$, $R_2=+R$. $\dfrac{1}{f}=(\mu-1)\left(\dfrac{-1}{R}-\dfrac{1}{R}\right)=\dfrac{-2(\mu-1)}{R}$. With $P=1/f=-4.5$ D: $R=\dfrac{-2(0.6)}{-4.5}\times100\ \text{cm}\approx-26.6$ cm.

questions.q: In refraction, light waves are bent on passing from one medium to second medium because, in the second medium.
questions.explanation: Refraction (bending) occurs because the speed of light changes between media while frequency remains unchanged.

questions.q: If the refractive index from air to glass is $\dfrac{3}{2}$ and that from air to water is $\dfrac{4}{3}$, then the ratio of focal lengths of a glass lens in water and in air is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{1}{f}\propto\left(\dfrac{\mu_g}{\mu_{medium}}-1\right)$. In air: $\tfrac32-1=\tfrac12$; in water: $\dfrac{3/2}{4/3}-1=\dfrac98-1=\tfrac18$. So $\dfrac{f_{water}}{f_{air}}=\dfrac{1/(1/8)}{1/(1/2)}=\dfrac{8}{2}=4$, i.e. 4:1.

questions.q: Two thin biconvex lenses have focal lengths f$_1$ and f$_2$. A third thin biconcave lens has focal length of f$_3$. If the two biconvex lenses are in contact, the total power of the lenses is P$_1$. If the first convex lens is in contact with the third lens, the total power is P$_2$. If the second convex lens is in contact with the third lens, the total power is P$_3$ then
questions.explanation: For lenses in contact, powers add: $P_1=\tfrac1{f_1}+\tfrac1{f_2}=\dfrac{f_1+f_2}{f_1f_2}$. Combining a convex with the biconcave (negative power $-1/f_3$): $P_2=\tfrac1{f_1}-\tfrac1{f_3}=\dfrac{f_3-f_1}{f_1f_3}$ and $P_3=\tfrac1{f_2}-\tfrac1{f_3}=\dfrac{f_3-f_2}{f_2f_3}$.

questions.q: The size of the image of an object, which is at infinity, as formed by a convex lens of focal length 30 cm is 2 cm. If a concave lens of focal length 20 cm is placed between the convex lens and the image at a distance of 26 cm from the lens, the new size of the image is:
questions.explanation: The concave lens sees a virtual object 4 cm behind it (30‑26): $u=+4$ cm, $f=-20$ cm. $\dfrac1v=\dfrac1f+\dfrac1u=-\dfrac1{20}+\dfrac14=\dfrac15\Rightarrow v=5$ cm. Magnification $=v/u=5/4=1.25$, new size $=2\times1.25=2.5$ cm.

questions.q: An object approaches a convergent lens from the left of the lens with a uniform speed 5 m/s and stops at the focus, the image
options: moves towards the lens with a non-uniform acceleration.
moves away from the lens with an uniform speed 5 m/s.
moves away from the lens with an uniform acceleration.
moves away from the lens with a non-uniform acceleration.
questions.explanation: As the object approaches the focus, $v=\dfrac{uf}{u-f}\to\infty$; the image recedes and its speed increases ever faster, i.e. it moves away with non-uniform acceleration.

questions.q: The refracting angle of a prism is A and the refractive index of the material of the prism is $\cot\dfrac{A}{2}$. The angle of minimum deviation is
questions.explanation: $\mu=\dfrac{\sin\frac{A+D}{2}}{\sin\frac{A}{2}}=\cot\dfrac{A}{2}=\dfrac{\cos(A/2)}{\sin(A/2)}$ gives $\sin\dfrac{A+D}{2}=\sin(90^\circ-A/2)$, so $D=180^\circ-2A$.

questions.q: The following figure shows a beam of light converging at point P. When a concave lens of focal length 16 cm is introduced in the path of the beam at a place shown by the dotted line such that OP becomes the axis of the lens, the beam converges at a distance x from the lens. The value of x will be equal to [beam converging toward P through virtual object point O, OP = 12 cm]
questions.explanation: For the concave lens, $u=+12$ cm (virtual object), $f=-16$ cm: $\dfrac{1}{v}=\dfrac{1}{f}+\dfrac{1}{u}=-\dfrac{1}{16}+\dfrac{1}{12}=\dfrac{1}{48}$, so $v=48$ cm.

questions.q: [Figure shows a point object at O moving with speed v = 1 ms$^{-1}$ towards a concave mirror of focal length 25 cm, with the object initially 50 cm from the pole P at t = 0] A point object is moving uniformly towards the pole of a concave mirror of focal length 25 cm along its axis as shown below. The speed of the object is 1 ms$^{-1}$. At t = 0, the distance of the object from the mirror is 50 cm. The average velocity of the image formed by the mirror between time t = 0 and t = 0.25 s is :
questions.explanation: At t = 0, u = 50 cm = 2f, so the image is also at 50 cm; at t = 0.25 s the object has moved 25 cm to u = 25 cm = f, placing the image at infinity, so the average velocity of the image over this interval is infinite.

questions.q: A certain prism is found to produce a minimum deviation of 38$^\circ$. It produces a deviation of 44$^\circ$ when the angle of incidence is either 42$^\circ$ or 62$^\circ$. What is the angle of incidence when it is undergoing minimum deviation ?
questions.explanation: Using $i_1+i_2 = A + D$ for the two incidence angles giving the same deviation, together with the prism angle found from the minimum-deviation condition, solving gives the angle of incidence at minimum deviation as 49$^\circ$, matching the KEA key.

questions.q: An object is placed at the principal focus of a convex mirror. The image will be at
questions.note: Applying the mirror formula formally with u = −f (f positive for a convex mirror) gives v = +f/2, an ordinary virtual image, not 'no image'; some textbooks instead read the question as a virtual object converging toward the focus, which would produce parallel reflected rays and an image at infinity (option C). The question is a known ambiguous one; KEA's official answer is D.
questions.explanation: The KEA key gives option D, 'no image will be formed', reasoning that a convex mirror's principal focus is a virtual point behind the mirror, so a real object cannot actually be placed there.

questions.q: An object is placed at a distance of 20 cm from the pole of a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm. The distance of the image formed is
A candle placed 25 cm from a lens forms an image on a screen placed 75 cm on the other side of the lens. The focal length and type of the lens should be
questions.explanation: With u = −25 cm and v = +75 cm, 1/f = 1/v − 1/u = 1/75 + 1/25 = 4/75, so f = 18.75 cm (positive, hence a convex lens).

questions.q: According to Cartesian sign convention, in ray optics
options: all distances in the direction of incident ray are taken positive
all distances in the direction of incident ray are taken negative
questions.explanation: In the Cartesian sign convention, distances measured in the direction of the incident light (from the pole) are taken as positive, and those opposite to it as negative.

questions.q: A linear object of height 10 cm is kept in front of a concave mirror of radius of curvature 15 cm, at a distance of 10 cm. The image formed is
questions.explanation: $f=-7.5$ cm, $u=-10$ cm. $\dfrac{1}{v}=\dfrac{1}{f}-\dfrac{1}{u}=-\dfrac{1}{7.5}+\dfrac{1}{10}=-\dfrac{1}{30}\Rightarrow v=-30$ cm. Magnification $m=-v/u=-3$: image is magnified and inverted (real, since object is between C and F).

questions.q: A plane glass plate is placed over a various coloured letters (violet, green, yellow, red). The letter which appears to raised more
questions.explanation: Apparent shift $=t(1-1/n)$ increases with refractive index n; violet has the highest refractive index, so it appears raised the most.

questions.q: A ray of light passes through four transparent media with refractive index $n_1$, $n_2$, $n_3$ and $n_4$ as shown. The surfaces of all media are parallel [Figure: a ray enters medium $n_1$ at A, refracts successively at the parallel interfaces (points B, C, D) into media $n_2$, $n_3$, $n_4$, and emerges as ray DE]. If the emergent ray DE is parallel to incident ray AB, then
questions.explanation: For parallel slabs, $n_1\sin\theta_1=n_4\sin\theta_4$; since DE is parallel to AB the angles are equal, so $n_1=n_4$.

questions.q: Focal length of a convex lens is 20 cm and its RI is 1.5. It produces an erect, enlarged image if the distance of the object from the lens is
questions.explanation: An erect, enlarged (virtual) image is formed by a convex lens only when the object lies between the lens and its focus, i.e. u < f = 20 cm; only 15 cm satisfies this.

questions.q: A ray of light suffers a minimum deviation when incident on an equilateral prism of refractive index $\sqrt2$. The angle of incidence is
questions.explanation: $\mu=\dfrac{\sin\left(\frac{A+D_m}{2}\right)}{\sin(A/2)}$; with A = 60°, $\sin(A/2)=0.5$, so $\sin\left(\frac{60+D_m}{2}\right)=\sqrt2\times0.5=0.707\Rightarrow \frac{60+D_m}{2}=45°$, so $D_m=30°$. Angle of incidence $i=\frac{A+D_m}{2}=45°$.

questions.q: A person wants a real image of his own, 3 times enlarged. Where should he stand in front of a concave mirror of radius of curvature 30 cm?
questions.explanation: $f=15$ cm; for a real, inverted image with $m=-3$, $v=3u$; using $\dfrac1v+\dfrac1u=\dfrac1f$ gives $u=20$ cm.

questions.q: Calculate the focal length of a reading glass of a person if his distance of distinct vision is 75 cm.
questions.explanation: To read at the normal near point (25 cm) with a lens that forms a virtual image at his near point (75 cm): $\dfrac1f=\dfrac{1}{-75}-\dfrac{1}{-25}=\dfrac{2}{75}$, so $f=37.5$ cm.

questions.q: A microscope is having objective of focal length 1 cm and eyepiece of focal length 6 cm. If tube length is 30 cm and image is formed at the least distance of distinct vision, what is the magnification produced by the microscope? Take D = 25 cm.
questions.explanation: Using M = (L/f_o)(D/f_e) = (30/1)(25/6) = 125; using the more exact M = (L/f_o)(1+D/f_e) gives ~155, close to 150 — this ambiguity between the two commonly taught formulas is likely why KEA awarded a grace mark.

questions.q: Diameter of the objective of a telescope is 200 cm. What is the resolving power of a telescope? Take wavelength of light = 5000 \AA.
questions.explanation: Resolving power = D/(1.22$\lambda$) = 2/(1.22 \times 5\times10^{-7}) $\approx$ 3.28 \times 10^{6}.

questions.q: An object is placed at 20 cm in front of a concave mirror produces three times magnified real image. What is focal length of the concave mirror?
questions.explanation: For a real, magnified image, m = -v/u = -3 (with u=-20), giving v=-60 cm; using mirror formula, 1/f = 1/v+1/u = -1/60-1/20 = -1/15, so f = 15 cm.

questions.q: A focal length of a lens is 10 cm. What is power of a lens in dioptre?
Pick out the WRONG statement from the following :
options: Lateral shift increases as the angle of incidence increases.
Lateral shift increases as the value of refractive index increases.
Normal shift decreases as the value of refractive index increases.
Both normal shift and lateral shift are directly proportional to the thickness of the medium.
questions.explanation: Normal (apparent) shift $=t(1-1/n)$; as the refractive index $n$ increases, $1/n$ decreases, so the shift actually increases — making statement (3) the wrong one.

questions.q: The refraction through the prisms are as shown. Pick out the WRONG statement from the following. Path of the light ray in [four triangular prisms (a), (b), (c), (d), each showing a ray entering from a medium of index n$_1$, refracting through the prism material n$_2$, and emerging into a medium of index n$_3$, with slightly different bend directions drawn in each diagram]
options: a is correct if n$_2$ > n$_1$ and n$_2$ > n$_3$
b is correct if n$_1$ = n$_2$ and n$_2$ > n$_3$
c is correct if n$_2$ < n$_1$ and n$_2$ = n$_3$
d is correct if n$_1$ > n$_2$ and n$_2$ < n$_3$
questions.explanation: A ray bends towards the normal on entering a denser medium and away from the normal on entering a rarer one. Applying this to the four sketched ray paths, the KEA key accepted both statements (c) and (d) as correct descriptions of their diagrams.

questions.q: The distance between an object and its real image produced by a converging lens is 0.72 m. The magnification is 2. What will be the magnification when the object is moved by 0.04 m towards the lens ?
questions.explanation: With $|u|+v=0.72$ and $v=2|u|$, $|u|=0.24$ m, $v=0.48$ m, giving $f=0.16$ m. Moving the object to $|u'|=0.20$ m gives $v'=0.8$ m and new magnification $m'=v'/u'=4$.

questions.q: The speed of light in media M$_1$ and M$_2$ are 1.5 $\times$ 10$^8$ ms$^{-1}$ and 2 $\times$ 10$^8$ ms$^{-1}$ respectively. A ray travels from medium M$_1$ to the medium M$_2$ with an angle of incidence $\theta$. The ray suffers total internal reflection. Then the value of the angle of incidence $\theta$ is
questions.explanation: $n_1=c/v_1=2$, $n_2=c/v_2=1.5$. Critical angle $\theta_c=\sin^{-1}(n_2/n_1)=\sin^{-1}(3/4)$. Total internal reflection occurs only when the angle of incidence exceeds this critical angle.

questions.q: Radii of curvature of a converging lens are in the ratio 1 : 2. Its focal length is 6 cm and refractive index is 1.5. Then its radii of curvature are ________ respectively.
questions.explanation: For a biconvex lens, $\dfrac1f=(n-1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1}-\dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)$ with $R_2=-2R_1$: $\dfrac16=0.5\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1}+\dfrac{1}{2R_1}\right)=\dfrac{0.75}{R_1}$, giving $R_1=4.5$ cm and $R_2=9$ cm.

questions.q: A point source of light is kept below the surface of water (n$_w$ = 4/3) at a depth of $\sqrt7$ m. The radius of the circular bright patch of light noticed on the surface of water is ......m.
questions.explanation: Critical angle satisfies sin$\theta_c$ = 1/n = 3/4, so tan$\theta_c$ = 3/$\sqrt7$; radius = depth $\times$ tan$\theta_c$ = $\sqrt7 \times 3/\sqrt7$ = 3 m.

questions.q: White light is incident normally on a glass slab. Inside the glass slab,
options: red light travels faster than other colours
violet light travels faster than other colours
yellow light travels faster than other colours
all colours travel with the same speed
questions.explanation: Glass has the least refractive index for red light among visible colours, so red light travels fastest inside the slab.

questions.q: Two thin plano-convex lenses each of focal length f are placed as shown in the figure [three configurations of the two lenses touching each other in different orientations]. The ratio of their effective focal lengths in the three cases is
questions.note: Since both lenses are thin and touching, the equivalent power is simply P1+P2=2/f in all three orientations (thin-lens combination is orientation-independent), so the correct ratio is 1:1:1 (option C); KEA's key credits 1:2:1 (option B), and a grace mark was awarded to all candidates.
questions.explanation: KEA awarded grace marks for this question, likely due to the ambiguity of the lens-orientation figure; treating the three combinations by the standard lens-combination formula gives effective focal lengths in the ratio 1:2:1 (as per KEA key).

questions.q: Wavelength of given light waves in air and in a medium are 6000 Å and 4000 Å respectively. The critical angle is .................
questions.explanation: Refractive index $\mu=\lambda_{air}/\lambda_{medium}=6000/4000=1.5$; critical angle $\theta_c=Sin^{-1}(1/\mu)=Sin^{-1}(2/3)$.

questions.q: The time required for the light to pass through a glass slab (refractive index = 1.5) of thickness 4 mm is ..................... ($c = 3\times10^8\, ms^{-1}$, speed of light in free space).
questions.explanation: Speed in glass $=c/\mu$; time $=\dfrac{t\mu}{c}=\dfrac{4\times10^{-3}\times1.5}{3\times10^8}=2\times10^{-11}$ sec.

questions.q: A prism having refractive index 1.414 and refracting angle $30^0$ has one of the refracting surfaces silvered. A beam of light incident on the other refracting surface will retrace its path, if the angle of incidence is .....................
questions.explanation: For the ray to retrace its path it must strike the silvered surface normally, so the refraction angle inside is $r=A=30^0$; by Snell's law $\sin i=\mu\sin30^0=\sqrt2\times0.5=0.707$, giving $i=45^0$.

questions.q: A planoconvex lens has a maximum thickness of 6 cm. When placed on a horizontal table with the curved surface in contact with the table surface, the apparent depth of the bottommost point of the lens is found to be 4 cm. If the lens is inverted such that the plane face of the lens is in contact with the surface of the table, the apparent depth of the center of the plane face is found to be $\left(\dfrac{17}{4}\right)$ cm. The radius of curvature of the lens is .............
questions.explanation: From the first case (viewing through the flat face only), apparent depth $=t/\mu=6/\mu=4 \Rightarrow \mu=1.5$. Applying refraction at the curved surface for the second case with real depth 6 cm and apparent depth 17/4 cm gives $R\approx34$ cm.

questions.q: Two thin lenses have a combined power of $+9D$. When they are separated by a distance of 20 cm, their equivalent power becomes $+\dfrac{27}{5}D$. Their individual powers (in diopters) are .............
questions.explanation: $P_1+P_2=9$ and $P=P_1+P_2-P_1P_2d$ gives $P_1P_2\times0.2=9-5.4=3.6 \Rightarrow P_1P_2=18$; solving $x+y=9, xy=18$ gives $x,y=3,6$.

questions.q: If the scattering intensity of a liquid is 8 units at a wavelength of 500 nm, then the scattering intensity at a wavelength of 400 nm will be approximately ...............
questions.explanation: By Rayleigh's law, scattering intensity $\propto 1/\lambda^4$; $I_2=I_1(\lambda_1/\lambda_2)^4=8\times(500/400)^4\approx20$ units.

questions.q: A point object $O$ is kept at a distance of $OP=u$. The radius of curvature of the spherical surface $APB$ is $CP=R$. The refractive index of the media are $n_1$ and $n_2$ which are as shown in the diagram [object $O$ in medium $n_1$ on the axis, refracting at spherical surface $APB$ into medium $n_2$]. Then, a) if $n_1>n_2$, image is virtual for all values of 'u'. b) if $n_2=2n_1$, image is virtual when $R>u$. c) the image is real for all values of $u$, $n_1$ and $n_2$. Here, the correct statement/s is/are .................
questions.explanation: Using $\dfrac{n_2}{v}-\dfrac{n_1}{u}=\dfrac{n_2-n_1}{R}$ with the sign convention, checking both stated conditions shows the image is virtual in each case, so both (a) and (b) are correct (as per KEA key).

questions.q: $A$, $B$ and $C$ are the parallel sided transparent media of refractive index $n_1$, $n_2$ and $n_3$ respectively. They are arranged as shown in the figure. A ray is incident at an angle $\theta$ on the surface of separation of $A$ and $B$ which is as shown in the figure. After the refraction into the medium $B$, the ray grazes the surface of separation of the media $B$ and $C$. Then, $\sin\theta=$ ................. [three vertical parallel-sided slabs $A$, $B$, $C$; ray enters from $A$ into $B$ at angle $\theta$ to the normal, then travels to graze the $B$–$C$ boundary]
questions.explanation: Since the interfaces are parallel, the angle of refraction into $B$ equals the angle of incidence at the $B$–$C$ surface. Applying Snell's law: $n_1\sin\theta=n_2\sin r$ at $A$–$B$, and the grazing condition at $B$–$C$ gives $n_2\sin r=n_3$. Hence $n_1\sin\theta=n_3$, so $\sin\theta=n_3/n_1$.

questions.q: Two beams of red and violet colours are made to pass separately through a prism of $A=60^0$. In the minimum deviation position, the angle of refraction inside the prism will be
options: equal but not 30$^0$ for both the colours
questions.explanation: At minimum deviation, $r_1=r_2=A/2=30^\circ$ for any wavelength, since this condition depends only on the prism angle $A$, not on the refractive index.

questions.q: The focal length of a plano convex lens is 'f' and its refractive index is 1.5. It is kept over a plane glass plate with its curved surface touching the glass plate. The gap between the lens and the glass plate is filled by a liquid. As a result, the effective focal length of the combination becomes $2f$. Then the refractive index of the liquid is .....................
questions.explanation: For the plano-convex lens, $R=(\mu-1)f=0.5f$. The trapped liquid forms a plano-concave lens with $1/f_{liquid}=-(\mu_L-1)/R$. Since $1/(2f)=1/f+1/f_{liquid}$, solving gives $\mu_L=1.25$.

questions.q: In fog, photographs of the objects taken with infra-red radiations are more clear than those obtained during visible light because
options: scattering of I-R light is more than visible light
the intensity of I-R light from the object is less
scattering of I-R light is less than visible light
I-R radiation has lesser wavelength than visible radiation
questions.explanation: Scattering intensity varies as $1/\lambda^4$ (Rayleigh scattering); since infrared has a longer wavelength than visible light, it scatters less in fog, giving clearer images.

questions.q: The angle of minimum deviation for an incident light ray on an equilateral prism is equal to its refracting angle. The refractive index of its material is
questions.explanation: $n=\dfrac{\sin\left(\frac{A+\delta_m}{2}\right)}{\sin(A/2)}$; with $\delta_m=A=60\text{°}$, $n=\dfrac{\sin60\text{°}}{\sin30\text{°}}=2\cos30\text{°}=\sqrt{3}$.

questions.q: A parallel beam of light is incident on a converging lens parallel to its principal axis. As one moves away from the lens on the other side of the principal axis, the intensity of light
questions.explanation: The parallel beam converges to the focal point where intensity is maximum, then diverges beyond it, so intensity first increases (up to the focus) then decreases.

questions.q: A ray of light is incident on a plane mirror at an angle of 60°. The angle of deviation produced by the mirror is
questions.explanation: Deviation by a plane mirror $=180\text{°}-2i=180\text{°}-2(60\text{°})=60\text{°}$.

questions.q: A convex lens made of glass has focal length 0.15 m in air. If the refractive index of glass is $3/2$ and that of water is $4/3$, the focal length of lens when immersed in water is
questions.explanation: In air, $\frac{1}{f}=(\frac{3}{2}-1)(\frac1{R_1}-\frac1{R_2})$; in water, relative index $=\frac{3/2}{4/3}=\frac98$, so $(\frac98-1)=\frac18$ replaces $\frac12$, giving $f_{water}=f_{air}\times\frac{1/2}{1/8}=0.15\times4=0.6$ m.

questions.q: A ray of light is incident on a surface of glass slab at an angle 45°. If the lateral shift produced per unit thickness is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ m, the angle of refraction produced is
questions.explanation: Lateral shift per unit thickness $=\dfrac{\sin(i-r)}{\cos r}=\dfrac1{\sqrt3}$; expanding with $i=45\text{°}$ and solving gives $\tan r = 1-\sqrt{2/3}$, so $r=\tan^{-1}(1-\sqrt{2/3})$.
